If you've been missing the ability to double-click the Digital Crown on your Apple Watch to bring up the app switcher — a feature that existed before watchOS 27 — it looks like that functionality is set to make a triumphant return in watchOS 27.2 beta 2. Details below.

Apple is working to bring back the watchOS app switcher

Apple pushed watchOS 26.2 beta 2 to developers this morning, less than a week after the previous beta 1.

Today's beta includes one detail that should please long-time Apple Watch users, including my colleague Zac Hall. Earlier this month, he wrote about how watchOS 26 removed the ability to double-click the Digital Crown to quickly switch between recently used apps.

He noted in his article that there was no longer a way to quickly jump between recent apps, and he hoped Apple would restore the gesture before the official watchOS 26 release, or in a future update.

While Apple hasn't yet restored the Digital Crown gesture to summon the app switcher in today's watchOS 26.2 beta 2, it has brought back the app switcher itself via a new gesture.

According to a discovery on the Apple Den Discord server, shared by user Bones on X, watchOS 26.2 beta 2 lets users summon the app switcher by long-pressing on the bottom of the screen while using an app.

As Bones notes in their post, the app switcher works much like it did before: after long-pressing the bottom of the screen to launch the switcher, users can rotate the Digital Crown to scroll through recently used apps, or swipe left on an app and tap the "X" button to remove it from the switcher.

As with any beta, there's no guarantee this particular gesture will make it into the final release (expected next month), but the addition in watchOS 26.2 beta 2 suggests Apple is listening to users and actively working on a way to bring back the app switcher.

Do you miss the watchOS 26 app switcher? Let us know in the comments.
